decisions.rationale: Lead Mamoswine and Armarouge to pressure Dragapult, Incineroar, and Metagross immediately while preserving strong spread protection through Armarouge's Wide Guard. Bring Archaludon as durable special pressure in the back, with Sneasler providing fast Fake Out, Taunt, and Coaching support.
decisions.notebook: Mamoswine plus Armarouge is a strong pressure core into this opponent's structure. Preserve Archaludon as a valuable backline attacker. Dragapult is vulnerable to Mamoswine's Ice Shard and should be prioritized early. Expect Klefki screens and Mega Metagross Earthquake; Wide Guard is valuable. Avoid relying on exposed Trick Room turns against pressure on Farigiraf.

decisions.rationale: Incineroar brings Intimidate, Darkest Lariat for Farigiraf, and Parting Shot pivoting. Dragapult is our fastest mon with Will-O-Wisp for Mamoswine/Sneasler, U-turn momentum, and Dragon Darts pressure. Rotom-Wash adds bulk, a second Will-O-Wisp, Hydro Pump for Armarouge, and Ground immunity. Clawitzer is the special wallbreaker: Mega Launcher Dark Pulse threatens Farigiraf/Sinistcha, Aura Sphere hits Mamoswine/Archaludon super-effectively, and Water Pulse covers Armarouge. Metagross is left behind due to Fire/Ground weaknesses into Armarouge and Mamoswine; Klefki's Prankster is blanked by Farigiraf's Armor Tail.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Dragapult, Rotom-Wash, Clawitzer. Opponent's Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority). Mamoswine is Thick Fat + Ground (immune to Thunder Wave, resists Fire/Ice). Armarouge has Flash Fire + Wide Guard. Sneasler has Focus Sash + Unburden. Sinistcha has Rage Powder redirection. Archaludon has Stamina. Clawitzer's Mega Launcher Dark Pulse and Aura Sphere are key for Farigiraf and Mamoswine/Archaludon respectively. Dragapult outspeeds everything and can burn physical attackers. Rotom-Wash is Ground-immune and can burn. Incineroar Intimidate cycles with Parting Shot.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Mamoswine)
decisions.rationale: Ice Shard pressures the fast Dragapult while Wide Guard protects both Pokémon from Dragon Darts and preserves the core against spread pressure.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize preserving Mamoswine plus Armarouge as a pressure core; Wide Guard is especially valuable against spread attacks and future Mega Metagross Earthquake. Preserve Archaludon as a valuable backline attacker, and prioritize removing or limiting Dragapult early.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult outspeeds Mamoswine and burns it with Will-O-Wisp before it moves, halving its Attack on top of the existing -1 Intimidate. This turns Icicle Crash from a possible OHKO (89.7-127.9%) into a safe 2HKO. Simultaneously, Incineroar Fake Outs Armarouge to prevent Wide Guard (which would block future spread moves) and Armor Cannon pressure. Even if Armarouge Protects, the burn still lands on Mamoswine. Farigiraf is not on the field, so Armor Tail does not block Fake Out.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Dragapult, Rotom-Wash, Clawitzer. Opponent's Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority). Mamoswine is Thick Fat + Ground. Armarouge has Flash Fire + Wide Guard. Sneasler has Focus Sash + Unburden. Sinistcha has Rage Powder redirection. Archaludon has Stamina. Dragapult outspeeds everything and can burn physical attackers before they move. Incineroar Intimidate cycles with Parting Shot. Clawitzer's Mega Launcher-boosted Dark Pulse and Aura Sphere are key for Farigiraf and Mamoswine/Archaludon respectively.

decisions.rationale: Clawitzer's Mega Launcher-boosted Water Pulse OHKOs Mamoswine (94-184%) and Dark Pulse threatens Armarouge (81-151%, possible KO from 87%). Clawitzer also has Protect for scouting and Aura Sphere for potential Archaludon. Rotom-Wash is safer defensively with Levitate but lacks the immediate offensive pressure to flip the 0-1 deficit. Incineroar must stay in to maintain board presence and threaten with Flare Blitz/Darkest Lariat.

Switch Mamoswine to preserve the pressure core and avoid its severe vulnerability to Clawitzer's super-effective attacks; Protect Armarouge to deny a likely double-target while bringing Archaludon safely into position for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mamoswine and Armarouge as the primary pressure core. Archaludon is a valuable backline attacker. Wide Guard is especially important against spread attacks and future Mega Metagross Earthquake.

decisions.rationale: Switch to Sneasler to preserve the Focus Sash and bring in a fast Fake Out user while Armarouge passes; this gives the best chance to regain tempo after Armarouge is likely targeted.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mamoswine and Armarouge as the primary pressure core. Sneasler's Focus Sash and high Speed can provide emergency tempo with Fake Out or Taunt. Wide Guard remains important for protecting against spread attacks, especially Mega Metagross Earthquake.

decisions.rationale: Both foes outspeed us. Mamoswine's High Horsepower into Incineroar does 66.8-96.5% (survivable with Sitrus Berry), and Armarouge's Expanding Force into Clawitzer does 37.6-53.9% (survivable). We retaliate with Darkest Lariat into Armarouge (57.3-105%, possible KO from 87%) and Aura Sphere into Mamoswine (85.3-163.2%, likely KO from 90%). Spreading damage threatens both slots; even if one foe Protects, the other takes heavy damage. This preserves both Pokémon and seizes momentum.

Sneasler acts before Incineroar and applies maximum immediate pressure with Close Combat, while Armarouge Protect prevents either foe from removing it this turn and preserves the core for the next turn.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mamoswine as the remaining endgame pressure option; prioritize protecting Armarouge when Clawitzer can threaten a super-effective Water KO.

decisions.rationale: Parting Shot on Sneasler debuffs its Atk/SpA and pivots Incineroar into Rotom-Wash, while Water Pulse on Armarouge forces the opponent into a dilemma: if they Fake Out Clawitzer to save Armarouge, Parting Shot succeeds and Rotom-Wash enters with Sneasler at -1; if they Fake Out Incineroar, Water Pulse KOs Armarouge anyway. Either outcome leaves us in a strong position with Rotom-Wash threatening both remaining foes.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Dragapult, Rotom-Wash, Clawitzer. Opponent's Farigiraf has Armor Tail (blocks priority) but not brought. Mamoswine is Thick Fat + Ground. Armarouge has Flash Fire + Wide Guard. Sneasler has Focus Sash + Unburden. Sinistcha has Rage Powder. Archaludon has Stamina. Dragapult fainted turn 1 to Mamoswine Ice Shard crit. Rotom-Wash is the only remaining bench; Parting Shot pivots are valuable for Intimidate cycling and positioning.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Sneasler acts first and pressures Clawitzer with Close Combat, while Armarouge must attempt Protect because either opposing Water move can remove it from 3% HP. This preserves Mamoswine as the remaining endgame pressure option.
decisions.notebook: Mamoswine is the remaining endgame pressure option; prioritize preserving it and protecting Armarouge when opposing Water attacks threaten a KO.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Sneasler cannot Fake Out (not its first turn out) so both my Pokémon will act. Clawitzer's +4 priority Protect guarantees it survives any double-target attempt; Sneasler + Armarouge doubling Clawitzer with Close Combat (52.8–75.8%) and Expanding Force (37.6–53.9%) could otherwise KO before Clawitzer moves. Rotom-Wash Volt Switch into the 3% Armarouge is a guaranteed KO (20.3–37.5% minimum), removing the special attacker. If Armarouge Protects at 33% success it lives, but Clawitzer remains safe and we enter turn 5 with both Pokémon healthy. This preserves a 2v2 endgame against Sneasler (Sash intact) and backline Mamoswine.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: brought Incineroar, Dragapult, Rotom-Wash, Clawitzer. Opponent's Farigiraf has Armor Tail but not brought. Mamoswine Thick Fat + Ground. Armarouge Flash Fire + Wide Guard. Sneasler Focus Sash + Unburden. Sinistcha Rage Powder. Archaludon Stamina. Dragapult fainted turn 1 to Ice Shard crit. Incineroar fainted turn 3 to Sneasler Close Combat. Rotom-Wash only remaining bench; Parting Shot pivots are valuable for Intimidate cycling and positioning. Sneasler cannot Fake Out after its first turn on field.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler's Close Combat pressures Clawitzer immediately while Mamoswine Protects from both opposing Water attacks, preserving the key endgame win condition. Clawitzer's reduced Protect success makes this the best balance of progress and safety.
decisions.notebook: Mamoswine remains the primary endgame pressure option; preserve it whenever opposing Water attacks can threaten a KO. Sneasler's superior Speed enables immediate pressure and Taunt against defensive or disruptive opposing Pokémon.

decisions.rationale: Double into Sneasler to guarantee a KO through Focus Sash. Hydro Pump (47.1–89.7%) breaks Sash, Water Pulse (58.3–111%) finishes; combined minimum 105.4% ensures Sneasler faints if Hydro Pump connects. Sneasler cannot OHKO either of our Pokémon, and Mamoswine's Ice Shard + Sneasler CC cannot KO Clawitzer before it moves. Worst case they double Clawitzer with High Horsepower, but even then Sneasler's Sash breaks and Rotom-Wash can clean up 1v2 with favourable matchups.
Sneasler is fainted, so pass. High Horsepower guarantees the KO on Clawitzer, removing the immediate Water threat and maximizing Mamoswine’s endgame pressure.
decisions.notebook: Mamoswine is the primary endgame pressure option; prioritize removing opposing Water attackers and preserve it when possible.

decisions.rationale: Clawitzer at 26% is threatened by both Icicle Crash and High Horsepower (guaranteed KO). Protect at +4 priority blocks any attack into Clawitzer. Rotom Hydro Pump into Mamoswine does 64.5-124.3%; even if it misses or rolls low, both my Pokémon survive to turn 7 where Clawitzer Water Pulse guarantees the KO. This line dominates: if opponent targets Clawitzer it's blocked; if they target Rotom, Clawitzer lives and KOs next turn; Ice Shard cannot KO either mon. Double-attacking risks Clawitzer fainting before moving, leaving a 1v1 where Hydro Pump may not KO.

reflections.summary: Lost because the four brought lacked a reliable answer to the opponent’s Rotom-Wash and Clawitzer core; once Archaludon and Armarouge were removed, Mamoswine and Sneasler could not finish through sustained Water pressure. The preview plan was only partly suitable: Sneasler was valuable against Incineroar, but bringing both Armarouge and Archaludon exposed too much of the team to Clawitzer and Rotom-Wash. No Mega Stone holder was brought or evolved.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, bring a dependable Water-resistant or Water-immune answer and prioritize removing or neutralizing Rotom-Wash and Clawitzer before committing Mamoswine as the endgame attacker; do not rely on Mamoswine alone to close while both remain active.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s demonstrated core is Rotom-Wash plus Clawitzer, using Hydro Pump pressure, Volt Switch positioning, and Protect to outlast attacks. Incineroar provides Fake Out and Intimidate support. Future plan: bring a reliable Water counter, pressure Clawitzer before it can use Protect cycles, and preserve Mamoswine until the Water attackers are removed or sufficiently weakened.

reflections.summary: won because Clawitzer’s critical Aura Sphere eliminated Archaludon early, and Rotom-Wash walled the remaining grounded threats with Levitate + Leftovers, while opponent's Wide Guard Armarouge lead offered no offensive pressure.
reflections.adjustment: start Rotom-Wash over Dragapult to avoid an immediate Ice Shard KO, and preserve Dragapult as a cleaner with Parting Shot cycling for Intimidate.
reflections.notebook: Opponent benched Farigiraf (Trick Room, Armor Tail, Mental Herb) and Sinistcha (Rage Powder, Hospitality) in game 2, likely expecting a fast mode. Armarouge carried Wide Guard, possibly to block anticipated spread moves. Mamoswine's Ice Shard is a priority threat to Dragapult. Sneasler holds Focus Sash and snowballs with Unburden + Close Combat drops. Archaludon’s Expert Belt + Stamina is special; Rotom’s Levitate avoids High Horsepower. If opponent reverts to Trick Room in game 3, bring Farigiraf checks and consider preserving Incineroar’s Parting Shot to pivot out of room.
